title: How many perfect squares lie between one hundred one and two hundred?
description: The video counts the perfect squares in the block from one hundred one to two hundred, and finds the largest square below one thousand. Keeko doubts the count after including one hundred, which sits just outside the block.
teaching_notes: One idea: to count the squares in a block, find the first square above the start and the last square below the end, and list the squares in between. Watch for students who include a square that sits on the wrong side of an end number.

source: How many perfect squares lie between 101 and 200, and what is the largest square less than 1000?
video_script.why: The child learns to count the squares inside a block of numbers by finding the squares just outside it, and to find the largest square below a number.
video_script.substitution: Find the square just below the start and the square just above the end, then list the squares between.
video_script.anchor: the block of numbers from one hundred one to two hundred, with an empty answer box
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko counts 100 = 10² as well and says five squares. But 100 is less than 101, so it lies outside the block 101 to 200; the squares inside are 121, 144, 169, 196.
video_script.payoff_line: There are four perfect squares between one hundred one and two hundred

final_answer.value: 4 squares; the largest square below 1000 is 961
final_answer.spoken: four squares, and the largest square below one thousand is nine hundred sixty one

hold_back: 4 squares; the largest square below 1000 is 961
never_show: the squares between 16 and 17 or 99 and 100 of the exercise video
maths_rules: the squares inside the block are 11² = 121, 12² = 144, 13² = 169, 14² = 196: 4 squares
31² = 961 and 32² = 1024, so 961 is the largest square below 1000
check: 961 + the 32nd odd number 63 = 1024, which is over 1000; 196 < 200 and 121 > 101
ground: block 10 to 40: 3² = 9 below, 4² = 16, 5² = 25, 6² = 36 inside, 7² = 49 above
the slip: 100 is below 101, so 10² is outside the block
video_script.design: One idea: the squares just outside the block mark the squares inside. Wrong idea: counting a square at the edge. The block stays in the anchor band and the squares fill in on the working board.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='term'/>A perfect square means the square of a natural number.
<bookmark mark='block'/>Look at the numbers from one hundred one to two hundred.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many perfect squares lie in that block, and which is the largest square below one thousand?

beats.on_screen: the question holds still and the empty answer box glows

marks.stop: the empty answer box glows in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a small block from 10 to 40: 3² = 9 just below it, 4² = 16, 5² = 25, 6² = 36 inside it, 7² = 49 above it

marks.below: 3² = 9 appears just left of the block from 10 to 40
marks.inside: 16, 25 and 36 light up inside the block
marks.above: 7² = 49 appears just right of the block

narration: <bookmark mark='below'/>Try a small block first, the numbers from ten to forty. Three squared is nine, which is right below it.
<bookmark mark='inside'/>Four squared, five squared and six squared are sixteen, twenty five and thirty six, all inside the block.
<bookmark mark='above'/>Seven squared is forty nine, which is above it. The squares next to the block, on either side, mark the squares inside.

beats.on_screen: Given: the block 101 to 200, and the number 1000

marks.given: the block and the number 1000 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the block runs from one hundred one to two hundred. There is also the number one thousand.

beats.on_screen: To find: the perfect squares in the block, and the largest square below 1000

marks.find: the two things to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to count the perfect squares in the block, and find the largest square below one thousand.

marks.ten: 10² = 100 is written just left of the block
marks.fifteen: 15² = 225 is written just right of the block

narration: <bookmark mark='ten'/>Step one, ten squared is one hundred, which is right below one hundred one.
<bookmark mark='fifteen'/>Fifteen squared is two hundred twenty five, which is above two hundred.
<bookmark mark='eleven'/>Step two, the squares inside are from eleven squared up to fourteen squared. Eleven squared is one hundred twenty one, and twelve squared is one hundred forty four.
<bookmark mark='thirteen'/>Thirteen squared is one hundred sixty nine, and fourteen squared is one hundred ninety six.
<bookmark mark='count'/>That is four squares.

beats.on_screen: 31² = 961 and 32² = 1024; so the largest square below 1000 is 961
narration: <bookmark mark='thirtyone'/>Step three, thirty one squared is nine hundred sixty one.
<bookmark mark='thirtytwo'/>Thirty two squared is one thousand twenty four, which is over one thousand.
<bookmark mark='largest'/>The last square under one thousand is the one before it.

marks.odd: 961 + 63 = 1024 is written, with 63 as the 32nd odd number

narration: <bookmark mark='odd'/>Step four, check the squares at the edges. Nine hundred sixty one plus sixty three is one thousand twenty four.
<bookmark mark='edges'/>One hundred ninety six is under two hundred, and one hundred twenty one is over one hundred one.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 4 squares; the largest square below 1000 is 961
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>There are four perfect squares between one hundred one and two hundred. The largest square below one thousand is nine hundred sixty one.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 100, 121, 144, 169, 196 are five squares; the 100 sits just left of the block and is crossed out

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble shows five squares starting at 100
marks.edge: the 100 is placed just left of the block starting at 101
marks.fix: the 100 is crossed out and the count changes to four

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks there are five squares, because one hundred is also a square.
<bookmark mark='edge'/>But the block starts at one hundred one, and one hundred is outside it.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Leave it out, and four squares are left.
